title: An Offering of Apple
story: James squeezed himself tighter into the shadow of the crates, his heart drumming a frantic rhythm against his ribs. The human was close now, so close that James could hear the heavy crunch-crunch of boots on gravel. He saw the patched blue fabric of the human's trousers. He saw the scuffed leather of the human's boots. He saw the low, sweeping shadow the giant cast across the dusty yard. When the shadow fell directly over his hiding spot, James felt the familiar tighten of panic in his chest. Instinct screamed at him to run back toward the safety of the Whispering Flats, but instead, he initiated his grounding ritual. He closed his eyes tight and listened. One: the dry, metallic scrape of a bucket being set down on gravel. Two: the soft, rhythmic sigh of the wind caught between the wooden crates. Three: the slow, deep breath of the human standing just inches away. When James opened his eyes, he was looking directly up into the face of a young human boy with a smudge of soot on his cheek. James had never seen a face so wide. He had never seen skin so smooth. He had never seen eyes so full of quiet, startled wonder. Neither of them moved. James thought of his lost metal ring, deep down in the dark iron grate, and wondered if this boy owned the grate, the yard, and the sky above it. Slowly, without making any sudden movements, the boy reached into his pocket. He did not pull out a net or a stone, but a small, wrinkled disc of dried apple. He gently laid it on the edge of the crate nearest to James, then took two deliberate steps back, folding his hands behind his back. The sweet, concentrated scent of apple mingled with the lingering smell of dust and iron. James reached out a careful grey hand, snatched the dried fruit, and held it tight to his chest. The boy gave a tiny, silent nod.
location: Behind a stack of wooden crates in the human yard
